title: On Defending the bridge for three days
subtitle: 战争和平 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 战争和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）
meta: 主题语境：战争和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）　|　核心词汇：defend　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 defend 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1962 the cook ① defended the bridge for three days before dawn, and every guest in the canteen said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the cook ② defends the bridge for three days in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ defend the bridge for three days at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ defended the bridge for three days before — a line in the menu for September 1956 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Defending the bridge for three days before dawn, the cook said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the bowl at the far table, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ defend the boy against every charge in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Defend the boy against every charge at once and never mention it again.

By 1969 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the menu, and a new guest from the next canteen ⑧ defends the boy against every charge before dawn every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the table, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ defended the bridge for three days again when nobody else would.

⑩ To defend the bridge for three days, my mother said in 1974, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the canteen remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the canteen forgets, somebody defends the bridge for three days in public again and somebody must defend the bridge for three days before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 保卫（一般过去式 defended the bridge for three days：1962 年厨子头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 保卫（一般现在 defends the bridge for three days：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 保卫（不定式 to defend the bridge for three days：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 保卫（过去完成时 had defended the bridge for three days：1956 年九月的菜单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 保卫（动名词 defending the bridge for three days 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 为…辩护（defend the boy against every charge：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去为…辩护替那孩子挡下每一条指控）
G. v. 为…辩护（defend the boy against every charge：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 保卫（后段两处：新来的客人照例 defends the boy against every charge，而母亲又一次 defended the bridge for three days）

answers.why: defend 意为“保卫”，1962 年厨子天没亮就保卫把那座桥守了三天，那是食堂里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 defended。
defend 意为“保卫”，自那以后厨子当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 defends。
defend 意为“保卫”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯保卫把那座桥守了三天”，此处为不定式 to defend the bridge for three days。
defend 意为“保卫”，菜单里 九月 那行字说明早在 1969 年之前就有人保卫过，故用过去完成时 had defended。
defend 意为“保卫”，厨子说“保卫把那座桥守了三天这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 defending the bridge for three days 作主语。
defend 意为“为…辩护”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去为…辩护替那孩子挡下每一条指控”，should ever 之后用原形 defend the boy against every charge。
defend 意为“为…辩护”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻为…辩护替那孩子挡下每一条指控（defend the boy against every charge at once），以后再也不要提起。
defend 意为“保卫”，新来的客人每个日子都照例为…辩护替那孩子挡下每一条指控，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 defends。
defend 意为“保卫”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就保卫把那座桥守了三天，用一般过去式 defended 叙述。
defend 意为“保卫”，结尾那句是母亲 1974 年的话：要保卫把那座桥守了三天，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和食堂记住的那一件。

多年以后，厨子仍当着众人面做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（defends the bridge for three days）

厨子说过，天没亮就保卫把那座桥守了三天这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（defending the bridge for three days 作主语）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 defend 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1962 the cook defended the bridge for three days before dawn, and nobody in the canteen forgot it.
Even now the cook defends the bridge for three days in public whenever the canteen asks.
Defending the bridge for three days before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever defend the boy against every charge in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new guest from the next canteen defends the boy against every charge before dawn every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother defended the bridge for three days again, and the canteen remembered that half.
